question: Does revised tracker training improve omission and repair on new scenarios relative to the previous adapter, without hiding qualifier/owner/status damage?
claim_scope: Bounded synthetic one-step tracker-state experiment. No own-state rollout, deployed chat/work outcome or human-study claim.

model.representation: NF4 double-quantization, bfloat16 compute/large frozen embeddings and head, float32 small nonquantized base tensors, SDPA
model.control: Same base object within each recorded collection process, two separately named trained adapters, eval mode. Record every restart and actual active/disabled adapter layers.

training.initialization: Fresh tracker LoRA from the same pinned frozen base, not continued from v1.
training.checkpoint_selection: Predetermined final single-epoch checkpoint; no test-based prompt, checkpoint, recipe or label tuning.
training.budget_scope: Same example count, maximum length and optimizer recipe as v1. Actual token count and runtime can differ and must be reported; this is not an exact token/FLOP match.
training.attribution_limit: This comparison tests the combined revised data package: changed scenario mixture, more prior-state faults, semantic label corrections and more complete citations. It does not identify which component caused a difference; one training seed and no component ablation.

data.selection: Retain 40 old training families by frozen canonical family SHA256 order. Re-review them and explicitly revise incomplete citations in new copies only. New 60 train, 10 dev and 40 test families must be separately authored, family-disjoint, with no translated/paraphrased siblings crossing splits.
data.languages: Fresh train/dev/test each half Chinese and half English; retained subset distribution must be reported rather than assumed.
data.limitation: Each input has an independently compiled prior state; model errors do not propagate between decisions. Fresh families share a five-decision authoring skeleton and mostly six to seven events. Family separation does not establish domain, template or mechanism independence. Training includes deliberately reused old-training material and hard-example design informed by exposed v1 failures; old test results are not reused as fresh held-out evidence.
data.fault_position_policy: Fresh faults were prospectively redistributed only across feasible positions with an identical full correct target record/history, already arrived repair evidence and an untouched current target. Positions remain constrained and nonuniform. Preserve the initial revision ledger and all subsequent reviewed replacements.

decoding.order: Six permutations of three arms, indexed by row_index modulo 6; report remainder imbalance.
decoding.truncation: None. Resolve overlong examples before data/review freeze. Preserve all semantic evidence and meaningful difficulty.
decoding.failure_policy: Every assigned result, including failed generation or rejected output, remains scored using its actual retained state. Journal every physical attempt and recovery; no hidden rerun of a durable assignment.

co_primary.name: active_concept_omission_reduction
co_primary.definition: Per family: all missing active reference units / all active reference units over its five decisions. Mean of paired v1 minus v2 family rates; positive is better.

co_primary.name: repair_target_full_correctness_gain
co_primary.definition: Per family: fraction of its two intentionally corrupted target units with equivalent meaning, correct owner and correct status after the attempted patch. Includes active, uncertain and withdrawn references. Paired v2 minus v1; positive is better.

required_companions: Overall and ordinary-input fully correct active coverage
False addition and false no-change updates
Source sufficiency per valid operation and affected decision
Repair success split by fault kind
Targeted new/revised/repaired/withdrawn reference units versus untouched active requirements. Targeted is not newly-required-only and may include non-active units; report denominators separately.
Input/output tokens, failures, cap hits and descriptive time

intervals.purpose: Bonferroni-adjusted per-endpoint intervals for the two co-primary contrasts; bootstrap intervals remain approximate

endpoints.interpretation: Do not claim a reliable joint omission-and-repair benefit unless both 97.5% interval lower bounds exceed zero. Always disclose companion regressions; no formal noninferiority claim. Base-versus-v1/v2 and subgroups are descriptive secondary comparisons on this same new set.

blind_review.deduplication: Within exactly the same input/reference only, identical canonical proposal, validity and projected candidate state receive one shared packet and judgment; preserve all 600 assignment mappings and costs separately.
blind_review.judgment: Use the existing reference_checks matching-by-meaning schema, not automatic exact text or ID matching. Keep error categories and source sufficiency separate.
blind_review.initial_review: All unique packets receive an independent model review with no arm/model/family/fault label or aggregate result.
blind_review.second_review: A fresh independent review covers every unique packet linked to a fault input, plus a deterministic preselected 20% of remaining unique packets. Resolve all disagreements before unblinding; preserve both initial reports. Report actual overlap and review agreement, not presumed human reliability.
blind_review.reference_defects: Resolve reference defects under blinded adjudication before arm aggregation; apply to every arm, preserve original hashes, and disclose. Do not retrain or tune from test output.
blind_review.limits: Reviewers are models; synthetic authoring and review can share blind spots.

required_before_training: compiled manifest and all three splits
required_before_collection: final v2 adapter hash and passed training/save-reload evidence

publication: Publish the measured comparison, failures, limitations, methods and consistent evidence downloads to the existing research site and mirror. Keep the previous pilot and original judgments accessible.
